uniequip_002_surtr:
'Sami blesses and protects us all. It is everywhere, and ever watchful over Its children.
'Every tree, every blade of grass in this tundra is part of It, and through them It guides us. Even in distant lands, It reaches through these mediums to aid us in troubled times.
'So what do you say? A handcrafted Sami spirit stone? Even the great Arges bought one, you know.' —A certain incorrigible Sami peddler
As Surtr, amidst the heart of the blizzard, prepared to leave the icefields' depths, Sami gave her a gift.
Slowly, the sheaves of frozen runes revealed to her melted, crumbled, and a stone of crystal ice fell at her feet.
As if compelled, Surtr picked it up, and found it not nearly as bone-chilling as its looks suggested. Even as the blizzard bathed it, it pulsed with a warmer rhythm. Almost a familiar one. The rhythm of life.
Such a familiar feeling. She looked at the sword in her hand, staring at the molten core within it.
Bringing the crystal to her sword, Surtr could feel... another self stirring, a voice crying out, 'Damn you, take that thing away! Get it out of my sight!'
So, Surtr bought one of those locally handcrafted Sami pendants, discarded its useless rock, and replaced it with the crystal. She wound the rope around the sword's hilt.
With every step forward, the pendant and hilt would knock together in rhythm—clank, clank. This annoyed her other self greatly, haughty yet powerless to resist.
In the back of her mind, Surtr couldn't help but laugh at it.
She knew it was a seething, scorching sort, easy to irritate, hated cold things the way one might hate the sound of nails on a chalkboard.
It was why she'd always loved ice cream, and all cold refreshments alike.
Clank, clank—Surtr knocked the pendant on the blade a few times, and it gave a few violent shakes in response, before settling down once more. The crystal's blue light bathed the blade's flame red, smothering it somewhat.
Thank you, Sami.
She could feel its blaze becoming wrath, increasingly unable to bear being slighted so, as if saying, 'You fool! You would choose this most pathetic, most damnable of means to get back at me!'
Nonsense.
She'd never considered its minor griping a threat, with or without Sami's help.
She's never seen her fiery powers as a blessing, nor has she ever felt restricted by the chaos that is her memory. Headstrong and self-centered, she disregards and cherishes as she sees fit.
Feranmut fragment? Big deal. Just shut it in front of me.
uniequip_003_surtr:
The first time Surtr set foot in the newly built Rhodes Island dormitories in Victoria, something in her felt hollow. A great deal had happened at Rhodes Island while she was away.
The new room set aside for Surtr was spare and tidy. Exactly as the message she had received before her return had said, they had simply moved her personal effects over from her old room without adding a single decoration. It was plain to the point of coldness.
Personal effects, in her case, meant her body monitoring equipment, a few articles of clothing, and some daily necessities.
Unexpectedly, though, a strange storage box had been left on the table in the middle of the room, impossible to overlook.
Surtr opened it and looked through the letters inside. Apparently it was full of gifts other operators had left for her over that stretch of time.

I heard you're headed for the freezing wastes of Sami! Please take this Rhodes Island self-heating travel mug with you. I've already tucked a recipe for a warming drink inside, so remember to keep the ingredients on hand so you can have some whenever you like!
—Hibiscus
'...I'm already back from Sami.'

I heard some time ago that Miss Surtr also can't remember things from before. This is a recording terminal I used to use. I know you're always on the move, so if you ever need it, please use it to write down the memories that matter.
—Rosmontis
'Rosmontis may have misunderstood what my memory trouble actually is, but I suppose this terminal would do for jotting down what I see on the road.'

Thank you for patiently running combat drills with me all those times, Miss Surtr. This is a portable ice maker issued only within Blacksteel. As long as you have batteries, it starts up very easily. I heard you're very fond of cold drinks, so I'm sure you'll find plenty of chances to use it while you're out traveling!
—Jessica
'Except there aren't any batteries in here... Though this chunk of ice I brought back from Sami fits inside just right...'

There was also a camping stove from Meteorite, a small travel pack from another operator, and all manner of odds and ends, which Surtr drew out and laid down one by one.
Looking at a whole table covered in things that seemed useful but, on reflection, weren't especially useful at all, Surtr found herself oddly pleased.
Surtr was not one for talking, nor one who took joy in helping others. She hated trouble. The girl she used to be rarely went out of her way to care about anyone—she could hardly keep up with her own affairs as it was.
And now, as a member of Rhodes Island, she had somehow come to be surrounded by this many people who cared about her.
An unfamiliar sort of relationship—but not an unwelcome one.
She left her usual terminal, her clothes, and the rest of her travel gear in the locker, and carefully parceled out the space in her pack for the recording terminal she had never used, the ice maker she wasn't sure would even work, the unfamiliar camping stove, the self-heating mug... She wanted to take them along. She didn't want to leave them sitting in the room.
She hefted the pack—hm, heavy. Surtr frowned.
From now on, wherever she went, she would be carrying the memory of the people who had given her these travel essentials.
